newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees world sugar prices falling to 10 cts/lb.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees world sugar prices falling to 10 cts/lb.

text.p: World sugar prices should drift lower towards the long-term average of 10 cents per pound as a 1996/97 surplus of 2.5 million tonnes weighs on the market, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Friday. But the bearish potential of the global balance could still be limited by a number of restraining factors, the ISO said.

These included the continuing tightness on the standard quality white sugar market, fears of a possible reduction of Brazilian supply from next year's crop, and the expectation of higher demand in the world market from Ukraine, it said.

"Nevertheless, we expect that the fundamental situation of surplus will eventually overcome these limiting factors so that the world market enters a period of lower prices, close to the long term average of around 10 cents/lb," it said.
It gave no time frame for the projected decline.
World prices for raw sugar are currently hovering under 10.80 cents/lb on the New York market for March delivery.
The ISO on Friday estimated world sugar production at 123.8 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, just 200,000 tonnes higher than in 1995/96.
This would lead to a global sugar surplus of 2.5 million tonnes, the second year of consecutive surplus and half the level of the previous crop year, it said.
